blocks.text: Buying an Acreage or ALR Estate in Pitt Meadows, BC

parts.t: With roughly 78% of its municipal land base protected inside the provincial Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR), the City of Pitt Meadows offers flat, scenic valley-floor acreages framed by the Golden Ears mountains, Pitt Lake, and 60+ kilometres of riverfront dikes—all within 5 to 10 minutes of urban shopping and West Coast Express.

Most Pitt Meadows acreages are located in North Meadows along Harris Road, Neaves Road, McNeil Road, and Rannie Road heading toward Pitt Lake and Swan-e-set Bay Resort & Country Club, as well as along Old Dewdney Trunk Road and Ford Road.

blocks.text: Pitt Meadows Acreage Due Diligence: A-1/A-2 Zoning, FCLs, Septic & Farm Class

parts.t: Under City of Pitt Meadows Zoning Bylaw No. 2505, 2011 and ALC regulations, rural acreage buyers must verify five key items: (1) principal and secondary residence floor-area limits and 'farm home plate' siting rules in the A-1 (General Agricultural) or RR (Rural Residential) zones, (2) Flood Construction Levels (FCLs) across the diked floodplain, (3) municipal water connection vs. private well and onsite engineered septic systems, (4) BC Assessment Farm Class income thresholds, and (5) building permits on barns, riding arenas, and workshops.

Are all Pitt Meadows acreages inside the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR)?

Nearly all rural acreage parcels in Pitt Meadows lie within the provincial Agricultural Land Reserve (which covers roughly 78% of the city) and are governed by both the Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) and City of Pitt Meadows Zoning Bylaw No. 2505, 2011.
What are the house-size rules on ALR land in Pitt Meadows?

Under provincial ALC rules and City of Pitt Meadows Zoning Bylaw No. 2505, 2011, principal residences and accessory farm residences on ALR land are subject to strict maximum floor-area caps and must be sited within a designated residential 'farm home plate' footprint near the road frontage.
Do Pitt Meadows acreages have municipal water and sewer?

Rural acreages in Pitt Meadows do not have municipal sanitary sewer and rely on private onsite septic systems (often raised mound systems due to the high water table). However, many rural roads in North and West Meadows are serviced by City of Pitt Meadows municipal water mains.
How do Flood Construction Levels (FCLs) affect building on a Pitt Meadows acreage?

Because over 85% of Pitt Meadows sits in the Fraser, Pitt, and Alouette river floodplains protected by 60 km of dikes, new habitable floor areas must be built at or above the municipal Flood Construction Level (FCL) using structural fill or raised foundations.
How does a Pitt Meadows acreage qualify for Farm Class property tax rates?

Under BC Assessment rules, an ALR parcel qualifies for low Farm Class tax rates when it generates qualifying annual gross farm gate income ($2,500/year for parcels between 1.98 and 9.88 acres, or $10,000/year for parcels under 1.98 acres) from crops, berries, hay, livestock, or qualifying horse boarding/breeding.
